h: The Shabbos Meal Restores Complete Faith and Eden

p: and that follows what is written
And it is brought (in the Zohar Chadash, beginning of this parashah):
one is the garden and one is the river;
this one goes out from Eden,
and that one is watered from it;
דְּאִיתָא בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב פח, א)
brought in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 88a):
and on the Field of Apples, etc."
שֶׁלֹּא שָׁלְטָה בּוֹ עֵין כָּל בְּרִיָּה
upon which the eye of no creature has looked."
they expounded "a field that Hashem has blessed":
"like the fragrance of a field of apples";
'He said to him, See, the fragrance of my son
is like the fragrance of a field.'"
And "river" is the entire middle line,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב קעה, ב)
as it says in the holy Zohar (Zohar II 175b)
that is, from Keser Elyon to Malchus,
And it is brought in the holy Zohar (Yisro, Zohar II 88a):
the head of Zeir Anpin is filled
with the dew that descends from Atika Kadisha,
and it casts it to the Field of holy Apples
after all, none of us knows the time,
וְגַם אֵין זְמַן אֲכִילַת סְעוּדוֹת שַׁבָּת
and moreover the time of eating the Shabbos meals
is not the same for everyone;
that at the time the Jew eats the meal,
and casts it to Chakal Tapuchin."
And this is why they are called
And as for its being specifically at a meal,
that the holy Ari, of blessed memory, called it
that the main purpose of the creation of the world
was for the Shechinah to be among the lower beings,
and that was in Gan Eden,
when he was expelled from Gan Eden
and although the Shechinah is in Gan Eden,
מִכָּל מָקוֹם אֵין זֶה נִקְרָא עוֹד
nevertheless this is no longer called
then the Beis HaMikdash was made
as the place of the resting of the Shechinah.
And after the Beis HaMikdash was destroyed,
it is the synagogues and study halls,
"'And I will be for them a small sanctuary' (Yechezkel 11:16)
these are the synagogues and study halls,"
And so it is expounded at the end of Shir HaShirim (Rabbah):
when he was in Gan Eden,
we do not find that he was commanded
וּמֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת טוֹב וָרָע לֹא תֹאכַל
"and of the Tree of Knowledge of good and evil you shall not eat,"
that "of every tree of the garden you may eat"
for about this it is written (Bereishis 2:15),
"to work it and to guard it";
'and to guard it' — with negative commandments";
we do not find that he was commanded any mitzvah.
And even the seven Noahide mitzvos
we do not find in the Torah explicitly,
when there was no yetzer hara,
לֹא הָיָה מָקוֹם לְכָל הַז׳ מִצְוֹת
there was no place for all seven mitzvos;
for there was no idolatry and no theft,
וְהַז׳ מִצְוֹת הָיָה רַק אַחַר הַקִּלְקוּל
and the seven mitzvos came only after the sin;
in eating, that it be in holiness.
And this is what is written (Bereishis 2:7),
"And He breathed into his nostrils the soul of life";
that is, "the soul of man is the lamp of Hashem";
the serpent and the yetzer hara can enter;
for this he was then commanded about eating,
when he ate from the Tree of Knowledge,
And regarding Shabbos it is expounded (Shir HaShirim Rabbah there):
אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל עוֹסְקִין בִּמְלַאכְתָּן
although Yisrael are occupied with their work
on the day of Shabbos they rise early
and come to the synagogue, etc.,
for on Shabbos all Yisrael are called
"you who dwell in the gardens" all day.
as it says (beginning of Seder Eliyahu Rabbah):
"On Shabbos one should make it entirely Torah:
and to the study hall, etc.,
and afterward go to his home
we see that even the eating and drinking of Shabbos
it is brought in the holy Zohar,
is from the side of the Tree of Life;
and as it says, "Those who taste it merit life";
and then all the words of Torah are
that the eating be in holiness,
as it was in Gan Eden
And therefore at the Shabbos meals
a person attains faith in completeness,
which are in the three meals,
